parsed.explanation: Combined regime: the national framework supplies the main traveller-facing exposure. Passport sex-marker restrictions are in effect, visa-stage discrepancies can lead to refusal and a possible lifetime fraud finding, and reported immigration-custody abuse of trans men is documented. The state layer is comparatively protective: no bathroom ban, no sex-definition law, sodomy repealed, marriage recognised, youth-care ban vetoed. It lacks statewide gender-identity anti-discrimination and hate-crime coverage, and national funding pressure has paused youth pharmacologic care. Universal document exposure with no operative remedy keeps this in the Elevated band, above the lower anchors but below reduced-risk tiers. The April 2025 trespass arrest is attributed to another state's statute and is not applied here.

entry_documents.exposure: National passport regime bars sex-marker change and X markers; the November 2025 Supreme Court order let restrictions take effect. Passports were reported confiscated or blocked, leaving some travellers stranded. Visa cable requires refusal on document discrepancy and raises lifetime fraud ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. Civil-liberties suit and litigation are unresolved; no operative visitor protection is recorded.
entry_documents.interaction: National rule applies at every entry regardless of state law. State laws do not pre-empt federal document or visa screening.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men. National corrections policies from 2026 mandate conversion-style treatment and hormone removal; population reporting stopped from 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State-level prisoner hormone entitlement (2011–2012 rulings) covers state custody only. No documented national custody protection.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor detained under national authority falls under the national regime, not the state's court-ordered hormone access.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars identity-congruent use of government-funded single-sex facilities. The state has no law barring trans people from government-building facilities, and the equality map lists no ban for this division.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No state facilities restriction documented. A 2019 state executive order bars gender-identity discrimination in state employment, contracting and services.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Whether the national order reaches state buildings is not documented beyond the map's caveat that other sex-defining policies may still affect access.

care_services.exposure: Two hospital systems paused youth pharmacologic care on 13 January 2026 after national payment denial. National subpoenas sought under-19 records. Proposed national rule would bar public reimbursement for under-18 care.
care_services.protection: No state ban on youth care; governor vetoed the 2023 youth-care ban. Mental and behavioural health continued; state joined a coalition challenge. Adult care not recorded as restricted.
care_services.interaction: National funding pressure overrides the state's permissive legal position at hospital level. Care continuity depends on individual provider decisions.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy prioritises neutralising 'radically pro-transgender' groups; a cash-reward scheme was set up. Federal directives target teachers using preferred names for prosecution.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State governor pledged to veto bills making the state less welcoming. Victim gender no longer recorded by one city police department. State bans on bathroom use or sex definition are absent.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal framing applies to all residents and visitors; state policy has not adopted the threat framing.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling minors face pharmacologic-care pause at the two systems, possible national record requests, and national sports and school-facing prosecution threats. A guardian may face inquiry if school-based name use is challenged.
minors_guardians.protection: State does not ban youth care. Governor vetoed youth-care and school-sports bills (2023, 2024). Athletic bodies retain their own policies.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor's continuity of care can be interrupted by national funding decisions even where state law is permissive.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence rate is documented. Hate-crime statute omits gender identity; prosecutors have used sexual-orientation framing. Local protection covers about 21% of population in full-ordinance cities.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Sexual orientation protected statewide in employment, housing, public accommodation and hate-crime law. Some cities cover gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Protection gaps fall on visitors in cities without ordinances; no documented police-response data for trans visitors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statewide gender-identity anti-discrimination law. Licence marker change limited; birth-certificate change requires surgery; no X option; name change restrictive. National marker regime and funding litigation are unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: 2019 executive order binds state agencies; marriage recognised since 2014; sodomy repealed 1983; local ordinances in some cities.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Document-based exposure at national entry is not reduced by state recognition or marriage rules.

anchor_checks.comparison: The 0.25-C anchor has birth-sex housing, cross-dressing arrests and solitary confinement as protection. This division has none of those state-level features, and its custody exposure is national, not state-run. Its documented harm is lower, but the national custody abuse reports keep it above that anchor.

The 0.45-D anchor has universal registration and nightly database exposure. This division has no comparable state registration system. The national passport and visa regime is a comparable universal document exposure, so the two sit at similar tiers, with this division somewhat safer for daily life.

The 0.55-D anchor has bureaucratic mismatch friction and no custodial risk. This division has similar document friction and entry refusal, plus documented national custody abuse and youth-care disruption, so it sits lower. Its absence of state facilities bans and protective state care law places it above the 0.55 level.

The 0.75-C anchor has respectful border practice, reasoned appeals and brief detention. This division lacks statewide gender-identity protections and faces an active national passport refusal regime, so it is clearly lower. Reaching 0.75 would require a national document regime that accepts visitor documents and an operative state or federal remedy.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets a national document regime that cannot be reconciled with a visitor's documents and may strand them. Visa-stage refusal and lifetime fraud findings add exposure. National custody reports of forced labour and abuse apply to visitors detained under federal authority, and the state's court-ordered hormone access does not reach that custody. The state's own record is comparatively permissive: no bathroom ban, no sex-definition law, youth-care ban vetoed, marriage and sodomy-repeal protections. Those mitigate the state layer but do not offset universal national document exposure or funding-driven care disruption. Remedies are unresolved litigation, not operating protection, so the combined regime sits in the Elevated band.
